title: Add profile drift detector and automated release-note suggester
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We frequently observe subtle performance regressions and config drift between successive onboarded model profiles that are only discovered after customer rollout. Manual changelog drafting is time-consuming and often omits the low-level telemetry signals that matter to SRE and product owners. This PR adds two related features: a profile drift detector that runs on profile snapshot timelines and an automated release-note suggester that turns detected deltas into human-readable candidate changelog entries.

Scope and behavior: The drift detector analyzes time-ordered profile snapshots for a model alias/variant and scores changes across latency P50/P95, memory RSV (KV-cache miss rate proxy), tokenization differences, and quantization-compat flags. It produces a small delta payload summarizing statistically significant shifts and an optional impact score. The autonote suggester consumes those deltas and emits templated release-note candidates with suggested severity (minor/major/regression) and recommended follow-ups (e.g., "reprofile with seq_len=1024", "pin quantized variant", "run eval-suite/production-prometheus-check").

Implementation details: 
- New module: registry/detection/drift.py — lightweight time-series comparator with outlier-resistant MAD-based significance tests and a configurable window size.
- New module: registry/autonote/suggester.py — maps delta signatures to prose templates; includes a small rule set and fuzzy-matching heuristics for tokenization/seq_len artifacts.
- CLI: `redwood-modelctl profiles detect-drift --model <alias> --since <date>` to generate deltas locally for debugging.
- API: profile-delta endpoint added to admin API (read-only, paginated): GET /v1/models/:alias/profiles/deltas?since=YYYY-MM-DD. The endpoint returns compact delta objects (timestamp, metric, old_value, new_value, significance, hint_tags).
- Backcompat: Detector is opt-in via registry config (profiles.drift.enabled=true by default in staging). No required data migration.

Commits (summary):
- 7f2d9c3: introduce basic MAD comparator and unit tests (drift.py)
- 48a1b2f: add delta schema and compact serializer for profile snapshots
- b3e4f6d: implement autonote suggester templates and CLI glue
- d2c8a11: wire API endpoint, add integration tests and docs

Files changed (high level):
- registry/detection/drift.py (new)
- registry/autonote/suggester.py (new)
- registry/api/v1/profiles.py (add delta route and serializer)
- cli/modelctl.py (add detect-drift command)
- tests/unit/test_drift.py, tests/integration/test_autonote_api.py
- docs/registry/onboard.md (new section: "Detecting profile drift and auto-suggestions")
- scripts/sample-data/profiles/sample_snapshots.json (test fixtures)

Tests / QA: Unit tests for the MAD comparator and template mapping are included (coverage ~88% for the new modules). Integration test spins up a small test fixture with three snapshots and asserts that the API returns a delta with the expected significance and a generated note containing the flagged metric. Manual QA: ran `modelctl detect-drift` against staging model snapshots and reviewed autogenerated notes for a handful of models; iterated templates based on reviewer feedback.

Performance and cost: The detector runs in O(n) per profile timeline where n is number of snapshots; the default window is 90 days and runs as a nightly background job. Memory overhead is negligible; initial benchmarks on staging (1000 model aliases) used ~150ms per alias when run in batch worker with cached profiles.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (staging): enable by default for staging; collect output and feedback for 1 week.
- Stage 2 (canary): enable for 10% of aliases in prod (config flag per-customer).
- Stage 3: enable for all aliases after fine-tuning thresholds and templates.

Security and privacy: Deltas only contain aggregated metrics and no raw prompt/content. API access restricted to admin scopes. Suggested notes redact any model-specific identifiers beyond alias.

Docs and UX: Added a short docs section describing interpretation of the impact score and a guide for integrating autonotes into the release process. We also added a small UI hook (placeholder) in the onboard console to preview suggested notes; UI work will be tracked in a follow-up PR.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Arjun Patel (review): "Nice work — the MAD approach is sensible for noisy telemetry. A couple of asks: 1) add a short test showing a tokenization-induced delta, 2) ensure the API returns stable IDs for deltas so they can be referenced in rollouts."
- Maya Chen (author): "Added tokenization test and stable-id generation using a deterministic sha1 over (alias, start_ts, end_ts, metric). Please re-review."
- Leah Rodriguez (review): "Templates are good; consider lowering default sensitivity for P95 to avoid too many 'minor' notes."
- Maya Chen: "Lowered P95 threshold to 2.5x MAD and added per-model override in config. Updated docs."
- Samir Gupta (approval): "Approach LGTM, test coverage good, docs helpful. Approved for canary."

CI: All CI checks passed after an initial lint failure (flake8: unused-import) that was fixed in the second commit. Integration job took ~12 minutes, full suite on main pipeline ~28 minutes.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main on 2025-11-18 after approvals and green CI. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-8794 for UI integration and ENG-8820 for threshold tuning.

Notes for operators: The background detector worker can be configured via `profiles.drift.window_days` and `profiles.drift.min_snapshots`. For urgent suppression, set `profiles.drift.enabled=false` in site config.

Related: This complements the onboarding change-tracking work (see ENG-8721) and will feed into the release-note aggregator for monthly release bundles.
release_notes: Added nightly profile drift detector and automated release-note suggester. Operators can run `modelctl detect-drift` locally; an admin API endpoint provides deltas. Opt-in rollout with canary config. No breaking changes.
notes_for_ops: Config knobs: profiles.drift.enabled (bool), profiles.drift.window_days (int), profiles.drift.min_snapshots (int), profiles.drift.p95_threshold (float). API access requires admin scope.
